thesis_title: Odporna detekcja anomalii w wielokanałowej telemetrii fizjologicznej: komitety losowych podprzestrzeni
thesis_statement: Komitety detektorów opartych na losowych podprzestrzeniach wykrywają anomalie w szumnej telemetrii fizjologicznej istotnie lepiej niż statyczny detektor Z-score, mierzone wyżej wartością AUC i F1-score przy zachowaniu niskiego ilorazu fałszywie dodatnich (wysoka Specyficzność).
baseline_comparison: Detektor bazowy: uniwariacyjny Z-score z progiem 3 sigma. Proponowana metoda: komitet N=20 detektorów, każdy trenowany na losowym podzbiorze D=3 kanałów, agregacja przez medianę odchyleń standardowych.

planned_chapters.title: Wprowadzenie
planned_chapters.focus: Motywacja problemu detekcji anomalii w telemetrii medycznej, zakres pracy i sformułowanie tezy.

planned_chapters.title: Przegląd metod detekcji anomalii
planned_chapters.focus: Omówienie metod statycznych (Z-score, IQR) oraz zaawansowanych (Isolation Forest, Autoencoders), uzasadnienie wyboru podejścia rozmytego/losowego.

planned_chapters.title: Propozycja komitetu losowych podprzestrzeni
planned_chapters.focus: Szczegółowy opis algorytmu: generowanie podzbiorów cech, lokalna detekcja anomalii, mechanizm agregacji wyników.

planned_chapters.title: Generacja danych i setup eksperymentu
planned_chapters.focus: Opis syntetycznego generatora telemetrii fizjologicznej (szum, trendy, anomalie), dobór parametrów i liczebności próby.

planned_chapters.title: Wyniki i analiza
planned_chapters.focus: Prezentacja metryk dla obu metod, w tym Specyficzności do weryfikacji tezy o niskim poziomie fałszywie dodatnich, analiza rozrzutu między powtórzeniami (std_dev) i dyskusja nad odpornością na zakłócenia.

planned_chapters.title: Wnioski
planned_chapters.focus: Podsumowanie osiągnięć, weryfikacja tezy i propozycje prac przyszłych.

interfaces.base_detector.py:
"""Implements the static univariate Z-score baseline detector."""

import numpy as np
from typing import Tuple


class ZScoreDetector:
    """Static univariate anomaly detector based on Z-scores.

    This detector calculates the mean and standard deviation for each channel
    of the input telemetry data. It flags a sample as an anomaly if the
    absolute Z-score in *any* channel exceeds a fixed threshold.

    The detector is 'static' because its parameters (mean and std derived from
    the fitting data) do not update during detection.
    """

    def __init__(self, threshold: float = 3.0) -> None:
        """Initialize the detector with a fixed Z-score threshold.

        Args:
            threshold: The number of standard deviations for a point to be
                considered an anomaly. Default is 3.0.
        """
        self.threshold = threshold
        self._mean: np.ndarray | None = None
        self._std: np.ndarray | None = None
        self._data: np.ndarray | None = None
        self._max_z_scores: np.ndarray | None = None

    def fit(self, data: np.ndarray) -> None:
        """Fit the detector by calculating statistics from clean data.

        Computes the mean and standard deviation for each channel in the
        provided `data` array. These statistics are stored internally and
        used during the detection phase.

        Args:
            data: A 2D numpy array of shape (n_samples, n_channels) containing
                clean telemetry data from which to derive the baseline statistics.
        """
        self._data = np.copy(data)
        self._mean = np.mean(self._data, axis=0)
        self._std = np.std(self._data, axis=0)

    def get_anomaly_scores(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Retrieve the anomaly scores computed during the last `predict` call.

        Returns:
            A numpy array of shape (n_samples,) containing the maximum absolute
            Z-score per sample across all channels. If `predict` has not been
            called yet, returns an array of zeros matching the data shape.
        """
        if self._max_z_scores is not None:
            return self._max_z_scores.copy()
        
        # If no predict was called, return zeros with correct shape based on fitted data
        if self._data is not None:
            return np.zeros(self._data.shape[0])
        return np.array([])

    def predict(self, threshold: float) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Detect anomalies in the data passed to the last `fit` call.

        Uses the data originally passed to `fit()` for detection. It does not
        accept new data as an argument because this detector is designed for
        a single pass over the dataset derived during initialization.

        Args:
            threshold: The Z-score threshold to use for this specific prediction
                run. Overrides the instance attribute if provided, or uses the
                instance attribute if not explicitly managed by the caller elsewhere.
                Note: To match the outline's explicit signature requirement,
                this method requires a threshold argument even if it defaults
                internally to the initialization value in some implementations.
                The contract demands `threshold` be passed.

        Returns:
            A tuple (predictions, anomaly_scores):
                - predictions: A 1D boolean numpy array of shape (n_samples,).
                  True if the absolute Z-score in *any* channel exceeds the
                  provided threshold; otherwise False.
                - anomaly_scores: A numpy array of shape (n_samples,) containing
                  the maximum absolute Z-score across all channels for each sample.
        """
        if self._data is None or self._mean is None or self._std is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Detector must be fitted before predicting.")
        
        safe_std = np.where(self._std == 0, 1e-10, self._std)
        z_scores = np.abs((self._data - self._mean) / safe_std)
        self._max_z_scores = np.max(z_scores, axis=1)
        
        predictions = self._max_z_scores > threshold
        return predictions, self._max_z_scores.copy()
interfaces.subspace_detector.py:
"""Implements the random subspace ensemble anomaly detector using Z-scores on random projections."""

import numpy as np
from typing import Tuple, Optional

# Ensemble configuration constants
N_ESTIMATORS: int = 20
SUBSPACE_DIMENSION: int = 3


class RandomSubspaceDetector:
    """An anomaly detector that uses an ensemble of univariate Z-score detectors on random feature subspaces.

    This class implements the core logic for generating random projections, computing local Z-scores,
    and aggregating them to produce a global anomaly score. It relies on reference statistics (mean and
    standard deviation) derived from clean, normal data to ensure robust anomaly detection even when
    the input signal contains outliers.

    Attributes:
        ref_mean: Array of shape (n_features,) containing the mean of normal reference data.
        ref_std: Array of shape (n_features,) containing the standard deviation of normal reference data.
        ref_data: Array of shape (n_ref_samples, n_features) storing the fit data to enable scoring later.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        n_estimators: int = N_ESTIMATORS,
        subspace_dim: int = SUBSPACE_DIMENSION,
        seed: int = 42,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the detector with ensemble parameters.

        Args:
            n_estimators: Number of random subspaces to use in the ensemble.
            subspace_dim: Number of features (channels) in each random subspace.
            seed: Random seed for reproducibility of subspace indices selection.
        """
        self.n_estimators = n_estimators
        self.subspace_dim = subspace_dim
        self.seed = seed
        self.ref_mean: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
        self.ref_std: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
        self.ref_data: Optional[np.ndarray] = None

    def fit(
        self,
        data: np.ndarray,
    ) -> None:
        """Fit the detector by setting reference statistics from normal data.

        Computes `ref_mean` and `ref_std` along axis 0. Stores `data` for use in scoring later.

        Args:
            data: A 2D numpy array of shape (n_ref_samples, n_features) representing normal reference data.
        """
        self.ref_data = data.copy()
        self.ref_mean = np.mean(self.ref_data, axis=0)
        self.ref_std = np.std(self.ref_data, axis=0)

    def get_anomaly_scores(
        self,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Compute anomaly scores for the reference data stored during `fit` using the ensemble.

        For each time step in the stored `ref_data`, computes the median of Z-scores across `n_estimators`
        random subspaces. Each subspace's Z-score is the mean absolute Z-score of the features
        within that subspace relative to the *global* `ref_mean` and `ref_std`.

        Returns:
            A 1D numpy array of shape (n_samples,) containing the anomaly scores. Higher values
            indicate greater deviation from the normal reference distribution.
        """
        if self.ref_data is None or self.ref_mean is None or self.ref_std is None:
            raise ValueError("Detector must be fitted before scoring data.")

        n_samples, n_features = self.ref_data.shape
        rng = np.random.default_rng(self.seed)
        subspace_scores = np.zeros((self.n_estimators, n_samples))

        for i in range(self.n_estimators):
            indices = rng.choice(n_features, size=self.subspace_dim, replace=False)
            projected_data = self.ref_data[:, indices]
            ref_means_sub = self.ref_mean[indices]
            ref_stds_sub = self.ref_std[indices]

            # Avoid division by zero; channels with zero variance in reference data are constant,
            safe_stds = np.where(ref_stds_sub == 0, 1.0, ref_stds_sub)

            # Calculate Z-scores using global reference statistics
            z_scores = np.abs((projected_data - ref_means_sub) / safe_stds)
            subspace_scores[i] = np.mean(z_scores, axis=1)

        return np.median(subspace_scores, axis=0)

    def predict(
        self,
        threshold: float,
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Compute binary anomaly predictions and raw anomaly scores for the stored reference data.

        Computes the ensemble anomaly scores using `get_anomaly_scores` and applies `threshold`
        to produce binary predictions (True if score > threshold).

        Args:
            threshold: The float threshold above which a sample is considered an anomaly.

        Returns:
            A tuple of two elements:
            1. Binary predictions of shape (n_samples,), where True indicates an anomaly.
            2. Anomaly scores of shape (n_samples), computed from the stored reference data.
        """
        scores = self.get_anomaly_scores()
        predictions = scores > threshold
        return predictions, scores
interfaces.evaluation.py:
"""Module for computing classification metrics and aggregating results for anomaly detection evaluation."""

from typing import Dict, List
import numpy as np
import sklearn.metrics


def compute_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray, scores: np.ndarray | None = None) -> dict:
    """
    Compute AUC_ROC, F1_SCORE, PRECISION, RECALL, and SPECIFICITY for binary anomaly detection.

    Takes ground truth labels `y_true` (0=normal, 1=anomaly), predicted binary labels `y_pred`,
    and optional continuous anomaly `scores`. `y_true` and `y_pred` must be of the same length.

    Returns a dictionary with keys:
    - 'AUC_ROC': float in [0, 1], Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve. Uses `scores`
      if provided; otherwise uses `y_pred`. If scores have zero variance or only one class is present,
      returns 0.5 (random guessing).
    - 'F1_SCORE': float in [0, 1], harmonic mean of Precision and Recall.
    - 'PRECISION': float in [0, 1], TP / (TP + FP). Returns 0.0 if no predicted positives.
    - 'RECALL': float in [0, 1], TP / (TP + FN). Returns 0.0 if no actual positives.
    - 'SPECIFICITY': float in [0, 1], TN / (TN + FP). Returns 0.0 if no actual negatives.

    Edge cases:
    - If `y_pred` has no positive predictions, PRECISION and F1_SCORE are 0.0.
    - If `y_true` has no positive samples, RECALL is 0.0.
    - If `y_true` has no negative samples, SPECIFICITY is 0.0.
    """
    metrics: dict = {}

    # Handle AUC ROC separately as it relies on scores if available
    auc_roc = 0.5
    if scores is not None:
        if np.all(scores == scores[0]):
            auc_roc = 0.5
        elif len(np.unique(y_true)) < 2:
            auc_roc = 0.5
        else:
            try:
                auc_roc = sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score(y_true, scores)
            except ValueError:
                auc_roc = 0.5
    elif y_pred is not None:
         if len(np.unique(y_true)) < 2 or np.all(y_pred == y_pred[0]):
             auc_roc = 0.5
         else:
            try:
                auc_roc = sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score(y_true, y_pred)
            except ValueError:
                auc_roc = 0.5

    # Use scores for thresholding if available (e.g., at best tpr/fpr or fixed threshold), 
    # otherwise use y_pred directly.
    preds_for_classification = y_pred if scores is None else (scores >= np.median(scores) if len(np.unique(scores)) > 1 else np.zeros_like(scores, dtype=int))

    # Calculate standard metrics
    f1_score = sklearn.metrics.f1_score(y_true, preds_for_classification, zero_division=0.0)
    precision = sklearn.metrics.precision_score(y_true, preds_for_classification, zero_division=0.0)
    recall = sklearn.metrics.recall_score(y_true, preds_for_classification, zero_division=0.0)
    specificity = 0.0
    if len(np.unique(y_true)) >= 2:
        try:
            tn, fp, fn, tp = sklearn.metrics.confusion_matrix(y_true, preds_for_classification).ravel()
            specificity = tn / (tn + fp) if (tn + fp) > 0 else 0.0
        except ValueError:
            specificity = 0.0

    metrics['AUC_ROC'] = auc_roc
    metrics['F1_SCORE'] = f1_score
    metrics['PRECISION'] = precision
    metrics['RECALL'] = recall
    metrics['SPECIFICITY'] = specificity

    return metrics


def aggregate_metrics(per_run_results: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """
    Aggregate metrics from multiple independent runs into final statistics.

    Takes a list of dictionaries, each containing keys 'AUC_ROC', 'F1_SCORE', 
    'PRECISION', 'RECALL', and 'SPECIFICITY' as returned by `compute_metrics`.

    Returns a dictionary with the same keys representing the mean across runs,
    plus additional keys '_STD' for each metric (e.g., 'AUC_ROC_STD') containing
    the standard deviation across all runs. If `per_run_results` is empty, returns
    zeros for all metrics and std devs.

    Edge cases:
    - Empty input list returns zeroed mean and std metrics.
    - Single run results in std_dev of 0.0 for all metrics.
    """
    if not per_run_results:
        return {
            'AUC_ROC': 0.0, 'F1_SCORE': 0.0, 'PRECISION': 0.0,
            'RECALL': 0.0, 'SPECIFICITY': 0.0,
            'AUC_ROC_STD': 0.0, 'F1_SCORE_STD': 0.0, 'PRECISION_STD': 0.0,
            'RECALL_STD': 0.0, 'SPECIFICITY_STD': 0.0
        }

    keys = ['AUC_ROC', 'F1_SCORE', 'PRECISION', 'RECALL', 'SPECIFICITY']
    aggregated: dict = {}

    for key in keys:
        values = [r[key] for r in per_run_results]
        mean_val = np.mean(values)
        std_val = np.std(values) if len(values) > 1 else 0.0
        aggregated[key] = float(mean_val)
        aggregated[f'{key}_STD'] = float(std_val)

    return aggregated
interfaces.score_exporter.py:
"""Aggregates and exports raw anomaly scores and ground truth labels for visualization support."""

import numpy as np
import os
from typing import Optional

# Output directory relative to workspace root (where experiment.py runs)
OUTPUT_DIR: str = "figures"
OUTPUT_FILENAME: str = "scores_for_plots.csv"


def export_scores(
    dataset_y_true: np.ndarray,
    baseline_scores: np.ndarray,
    subspace_scores: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
) -> None:
    """Save ground truth labels and anomaly scores to a CSV file for downstream visualization.

    The output file is written as `figures/scores_for_plots.csv` (relative to the current working directory, 
    which is assumed to be the workspace root).

    Args:
        dataset_y_true: A 1D boolean or integer array of shape (n_samples,) representing the ground truth labels.
            True (or 1) indicates an anomaly, False (or 0) indicates normal.
        baseline_scores: A 1D float array of shape (n_samples,) containing the anomaly scores from the baseline
            Z-score detector.
        subspace_scores: An optional 1D float array of shape (n_samples,) containing the anomaly scores from the
            random subspace ensemble detector. If provided, these columns are added to the CSV; otherwise, only
            ground truth and baseline scores are exported.
    """
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    filepath = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, OUTPUT_FILENAME)

    if subspace_scores is not None:
        header = "y_true,base_scores,subspace_scores"
        data_to_write = np.column_stack((dataset_y_true, baseline_scores, subspace_scores))
    else:
        header = "y_true,base_scores"
        data_to_write = np.column_stack((dataset_y_true, baseline_scores))

    np.savetxt(filepath, data_to_write, delimiter=",", header=header, comments="", fmt="%s")
interfaces.experiment.py:
"""Orchestrates the repeated experiments for both methods and writes results.csv."""

import os
from typing import Dict, List

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from data_generation import generate_dataset, SAMPLE_LENGTH
from base_detector import ZScoreDetector
from subspace_detector import RandomSubspaceDetector
from evaluation import compute_metrics, aggregate_metrics
from score_exporter import export_scores

NUM_RUNS: int = 10
ANOMALIES_PER_SAMPLE: int = 5
BASELINE_THRESHOLD: float = 3.0
OUTPUT_PATH: str = "results.csv"


def run_experiment() -> None:
    """Orchestrate the full experiment pipeline and write results to CSV.

    This function performs the following steps for each of `NUM_RUNS` independent iterations:
    1. Generates synthetic telemetry data with injected anomalies using `generate_dataset`.
    2. Identifies clean (non-anomalous) samples from the generated data.
    3. Fits the `ZScoreDetector` on clean data and predicts on the full dataset to obtain
       baseline metrics via `compute_metrics`.
    4. Fits the `RandomSubspaceDetector` on clean data, computes anomaly scores,
       determines predictions using a fixed threshold, and calculates metrics via `compute_metrics`.
    5. Aggregates metrics across runs using `aggregate_metrics`.
    6. Exports raw scores via `export_scores` for visualization support.
    7. Writes aggregated results to `results.csv` with columns: method, metric, value,
       std_dev (if applicable), n_runs.

    Side Effects:
    - Creates `figures/` directory and writes `scores_for_plots.csv` inside it.
    - Writes `results.csv` in the current working directory.

    Edge Cases:
    - If no clean data is found for fitting, raises ValueError.
    - Ensures deterministic results by seeding each run independently.
    """
    all_base_results: List[Dict[str, float]] = []
    all_subspace_results: List[Dict[str, float]] = []

    last_y_true: np.ndarray | None = None
    last_base_scores: np.ndarray | None = None
    last_subspace_scores: np.ndarray | None = None

    os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)

    for i in range(NUM_RUNS):
        run_seed = 42 + i
        
        telemetry, labels = generate_dataset(
            n_samples=SAMPLE_LENGTH,
            n_anomalies=ANOMALIES_PER_SAMPLE,
            seed=run_seed
        )

        clean_indices = np.where(~labels)[0]
        clean_data = telemetry[clean_indices]

        if len(clean_data) == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Run {i}: No clean data found for fitting.")

        # Baseline Detector
        base_detector = ZScoreDetector(threshold=BASELINE_THRESHOLD)
        base_detector.fit(clean_data)
        y_pred_base, base_scores = base_detector.predict(BASELINE_THRESHOLD)
        
        metrics_base = compute_metrics(
            y_true=labels.astype(int), 
            y_pred=y_pred_base, 
            scores=base_scores
        )
        all_base_results.append(metrics_base)

        # Subspace Detector
        subspace_detector = RandomSubspaceDetector(seed=run_seed)
        subspace_detector.fit(clean_data)
        subspace_scores = subspace_detector.get_anomaly_scores()
        
        # Use BASELINE_THRESHOLD for subspace as well for fair comparison if scores are comparable,
        # or use a threshold derived from the distribution. The prompt implies comparing against Z-score.
        # Let's use a fixed threshold similar to Z-score logic (e.g., 3.0) if scores are Z-scores-like,
        # but since subspace_scores are medians of absolute Z-scores, they might be scaled differently.
        # However, the interface contract for predict takes a threshold. We will use BASELINE_THRESHOLD
        # as requested in previous valid attempts to maintain consistency with the plan's intent.
        y_pred_subspace, _ = subspace_detector.predict(threshold=BASELINE_THRESHOLD)
        
        metrics_subspace = compute_metrics(
            y_true=labels.astype(int), 
            y_pred=y_pred_subspace, 
            scores=subspace_scores
        )
        all_subspace_results.append(metrics_subspace)

        last_y_true = labels.copy()
        last_base_scores = base_scores.copy()
        last_subspace_scores = subspace_scores.copy()

    agg_base = aggregate_metrics(all_base_results)
    agg_subspace = aggregate_metrics(all_subspace_results)

    csv_rows: List[Dict[str, str | float | int]] = []
    main_metrics = ['AUC_ROC', 'F1_SCORE', 'PRECISION', 'RECALL', 'SPECIFICITY']
    
    for method_name, agg_dict in [("ZScore", agg_base), ("SubspaceEnsemble", agg_subspace)]:
        for metric in main_metrics:
            mean_val = agg_dict.get(metric, 0.0)
            std_val = agg_dict.get(f'{metric}_STD', 0.0)
            csv_rows.append({
                "method": method_name,
                "metric": metric,
                "value": float(mean_val),
                "std_dev": float(std_val),
                "n_runs": NUM_RUNS
            })

    df = pd.DataFrame(csv_rows)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUTPUT_PATH) if os.path.dirname(OUTPUT_PATH) else '.', exist_ok=True)
    df.to_csv(OUTPUT_PATH, index=False)

    if last_y_true is not None and last_base_scores is not None:
        export_scores(
            dataset_y_true=last_y_true,
            baseline_scores=last_base_scores,
            subspace_scores=last_subspace_scores
        )

chapters.title: Wprowadzenie
chapters.focus: Motywacja problemu detekcji anomalii w telemetrii medycznej, zakres pracy i sformułowanie tezy.

chapters.title: Przegląd metod detekcji anomalii
chapters.focus: Omówienie metod statycznych (Z-score, IQR) oraz zaawansowanych (Isolation Forest, Autoencoders), uzasadnienie wyboru podejścia rozmytego/losowego.

chapters.title: Propozycja komitetu losowych podprzestrzeni
chapters.focus: Szczegółowy opis algorytmu: generowanie podzbiorów cech, lokalna detekcja anomalii, mechanizm agregacji wyników.

chapters.title: Generacja danych i setup eksperymentu
chapters.focus: Opis syntetycznego generatora telemetrii fizjologicznej (szum, trendy, anomalie), dobór parametrów i liczebności próby.

chapters.title: Wyniki i analiza
chapters.focus: Prezentacja metryk dla obu metod, w tym Specyficzności do weryfikacji tezy o niskim poziomie fałszywie dodatnich, analiza rozrzutu między powtórzeniami (std_dev) i dyskusja nad odpornością na zakłócenia.

chapters.title: Wnioski
chapters.focus: Podsumowanie osiągnięć, weryfikacja tezy i propozycje prac przyszłych.
